- Give FSDP `dp_replicate`, `edp_shard`, and flattened `dp_shard * cp` axes dedicated process groups, preserving the configured backend and FSDP2 mesh semantics.
- Add pure-CP/pure-DDP communicator-identity tests and an 82-line manual NCCL ordering probe.
- Four-B300 diagnostic: shared PG 0 / sequence 3 watchdogs; separate communicators complete with exact outputs on all four ranks. This deliberately reverses **host submission order**; completion is measured here, not a general reversed-order guarantee ([NVIDIA contract](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/archives/nccl_2307/user-guide/docs/usage/communicators.html#using-multiple-nccl-communicators-concurrently)).
- Continues #5645 under this account; Pei's original commits and authorship are preserved.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and measured setup</summary>

Exact tested source: [`2d52ccd1`, fault at line 56](https://github.com/tranle-fw/torchtitan/blob/2d52ccd11154378749428c01673b32c496914950/scripts/repro_collective_order.py#L56). Both runs used the same four B300 GPUs and PyTorch `2.13.0a0+8145d630e8.nv26.06`, CUDA 13.3, NCCL 2.30.5.

Run each case in a separate process/container with an external deadline. Equivalent local invocations with the recorded communication settings:

```bash
export NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1
export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_CUMEM_HOST_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo NCCL_DEBUG=WARN TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=0

timeout --signal=KILL 150s torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 scripts/repro_collective_order.py
timeout --signal=KILL 150s torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 scripts/repro_collective_order.py --separate-group
```

The measured runs used a container deadline and a CUDA-readiness gate before process-group creation; neither changes the script's fault phase. No GPU delay is injected. Source SHA256: `fb0abc0ec4a74a099a8f89125bf71e270cd9092253191f4c7e62aea79f6e88be`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Fresh run of the exact script: sanitized forced-order logs</summary>

Four CUDA ranks; PyTorch 2.13.0a0, CUDA 13.3, NCCL 2.30.5; `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1` in both runs. After matching AG→A2A warmup, rank 0 deliberately submits A2A→AG while peers submit AG→A2A. This is a host-order negative control, not GPU-only skew or a natural FSDP prefetch reproduction. Host/process identifiers, timestamps, paths and addresses are omitted; retained lines/payloads below are unchanged.

Shared group: all ranks warm up and both asynchronous calls return on every rank, then collective sequence 3 times out.

```text
rank=0 WARMED
rank=0 warmup=False submitted=a2a
rank=0 warmup=False submitted=ag
rank=2 WARMED
rank=3 WARMED
rank=2 warmup=False submitted=ag
rank=3 warmup=False submitted=ag
rank=2 warmup=False submitted=a2a
rank=3 warmup=False submitted=a2a
rank=1 WARMED
rank=1 warmup=False submitted=ag
rank=1 warmup=False submitted=a2a
[Rank 3] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=3, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=1048576, NumelOut=4194304, Timeout(ms)=30000)
[Rank 2] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=3, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=1048576, NumelOut=4194304, Timeout(ms)=30000)
[Rank 0] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=3, OpType=ALLTOALL_BASE, NumelIn=1048576, NumelOut=1048576, Timeout(ms)=30000)
[Rank 1] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=3, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=1048576, NumelOut=4194304, Timeout(ms)=30000)
```

Dedicated all-gather group: the same opposite host order completes. `PASS` is printed after CUDA synchronization and exact checks of both outputs.

```text
rank=2 PASS
rank=0 PASS
rank=1 PASS
rank=3 PASS
```

The shared run recorded the 30-second watchdog, then required its external 150-second container deadline (exit 137). The dedicated run exited 0 in 16.090 seconds. Dedicated completion is an empirical result of this test, not a general guarantee for reversed cross-communicator order.

</details>

@tranle-fw thanks for the mini-repro. I understand order issue so I think the mini-repro script is correct. What I want to understand is what TorchTitan's command, parallelisms setting make you discovered such an issue? I would like to know why we didn't discover this issue even though we have done CP only several times. Thanks! 

Also, please sign the CLA

Thanks for the response @fegin

re: command & parallelism setting, we use normal `torchrun` with our internal implementations of CP. From my experience, if the parallelism use p2p collectives, it'll more likely trigger the issue. We have production jobs running for months before triggering this hang, so it's incredibly hard to reproduce. 

Bug is triggered only when CP/FSDP span the whole world size which then shares the default pg (communicator).

**Claude finished @fegin's task in 3m 17s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41011708537)

---
**Request changes**: the PR hasn't shown the bug on torchtitan `main`, and its stream-based root-cause explanation doesn't match how a single NCCL communicator orders work. See the [review](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5663#pullrequestreview).

**Verdict: Request changes** -- the PR hasn't shown that the bug exists in torchtitan on `main`, and its explanation of the root cause doesn't match how a single NCCL communicator orders work. Isolating the groups could also bring in the cross-communicator ordering risk that the NVIDIA doc warns about.

**What this PR does.** When a mesh axis spans every rank, `DeviceMesh` reuses the WORLD process group instead of creating a new one. This PR passes an explicit `backend_override` so that FSDP's `dp_replicate`, `edp_shard`, and flattened `dp_shard*cp` axes get dedicated process groups. It pre-flattens `dp_shard_cp` under the name FSDP2 will use later, so FSDP2 picks the dedicated group out of the cache. It also adds two CPU tests and a manual NCCL probe script.

**Example.** `cp=4, dp_shard=dp_replicate=tp=pp=1` on 4 GPUs:
```
main: cp axis -> WORLD; FSDP shard axis dp_shard*cp (size 4) -> WORLD   (one communicator)
PR:   cp axis -> WORLD; FSDP shard axis -> new 4-rank PG                (two communicators)
```
The repro deadlocks only because rank 0 is forced to submit A2A->AG on the host while the other ranks submit AG->A2A. Torchtitan never does this, because its host order is the same on every rank. @fegin has run CP8 and CP16 with `dp_shard=1` many times without a hang. The author's answer is that the hang shows up with an *internal* CP implementation that uses P2P.

### Must fix
1. **The problem isn't shown on `main`.** @fegin's question ("what TorchTitan command / parallelisms") is still open: the only reported trigger is an out-of-tree CP. If that CP issues collectives in a rank-dependent host order (from a thread, data-dependent P2P, or lazily created P2P communicators), the fix belongs there. Please give either a torchtitan config that hangs, or an NCCL/flight-recorder trace from the production hang showing the mismatched sequence numbers across ranks.
2. `torchtitan/distributed/parallelism_context.py:95-100` -- the stream-based rationale is incorrect: the stream a collective is issued from doesn't change its host enqueue order, and one communicator serializes its work in launch order (inline).
3. **The fix may just move the hazard.** Once the groups are separate, the GPU order of FSDP and CP kernels really can differ across ranks. The linked NVIDIA doc says that can deadlock unless launch order is consistent or `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT` is set, and both measured runs set `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1` (inline on the script).
4. `torchtitan/distributed/parallelism_context.py:77-80` -- the `dp_replicate` and `edp_shard` overrides don't address the CP case. The `dp_replicate` one adds a world-size communicator under pure DDP; the `edp_shard` one is a no-op (inline).
5. `torchtitan/distributed/fsdp.py:145-150` -- the fix depends on FSDP2's private flatten naming and on `DeviceMesh` caching by name, with no upstream TODO or issue (inline).
6. `scripts/repro_collective_order.py` -- remove it; it's a probe of documented NCCL behavior with no consumer in the repo (inline).

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_parallelism_context.py:22-25` -- the test re-derives the FSDP shard group using private FSDP2 helpers (inline).
- `parallelism_context.py:37-44` -- re-sorting `__all__` is unrelated to the fix.

### Questions
- In the production hang, which collectives were at the mismatched sequence number on each rank? Were both on PG 0, and was one of them a P2P op from the internal CP?
- If isolation is still wanted after (1) is answered, should a dedicated FSDP group become an option in FSDP2/DeviceMesh upstream rather than a pre-flatten trick here?

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Host order within one PG: FSDP2's pre-forward/pre-backward hooks and CP's attention collectives run on the main Python thread in the same program order on every rank. ProcessGroupNCCL launches every op of a PG on that PG's NCCL stream, waiting on the caller's current stream. Issuing from `all_gather_stream` instead of the compute stream changes the dependency, not the sequence number.
- If the change is still wanted after the root cause is established, the smallest version is just the `fsdp.py` pre-flatten with a TODO linking an upstream issue (~10 lines), with no `_FSDP_SINGLE_AXIS_NAMES`, no DDP test, and no script.
- After this PR, CP's `cp` axis still shares WORLD with `loss_mesh` (dp*cp) and grad-norm reductions. That is fine under same-order host submission, and it is the same argument for why the FSDP/CP share is fine as well.

</details>

Not verified: NCCL-internal serialization of one communicator across user streams; DeviceMesh flatten-cache behavior on the pinned torch; no GPU runs. A maintainer still needs to review.

This explanation doesn't follow. The CUDA stream a collective is issued *from* has no effect on its *host* enqueue order. Host order is program order, and in torchtitan that's identical on every rank (FSDP hooks and CP calls run in the same Python sequence everywhere). For a single process group, ProcessGroupNCCL launches every collective on that PG's own NCCL stream, and NCCL serializes the operations of one communicator in launch order. So two collectives on one communicator can't be reordered on the GPU differently per rank. That's why the repro script has to force rank 0 to submit A2A before AG on the host.

If this docstring and the test docstring stay, they will teach a false model of NCCL semantics. Please either show the concrete rank-dependent host ordering that happens in a real run, or restate the rationale. *(unverified: the NCCL-internal serialization detail; a NCCL debug trace from the production hang would settle it.)*

@@ -66,6 +67,46 @@ class MeshAxisName(StrEnum):
     EDP_SHARD = "edp_shard"
 
 
+# Axes that FSDP/HSDP can use as a complete shard or replicate group on their
+# own (i.e. without being combined with another axis first). When one of these
+# spans every rank -- most commonly ``dp_replicate`` under pure DDP, or
+# ``edp_shard`` when EP leaves no other sparse-region parallelism -- it must
+# not be allowed to collapse onto the default/WORLD process group the way
+# ``DeviceMesh._init_one_process_group`` does for any full-world dimension by
+# default. See ``dedicated_pg_backend_override`` for why.
+_FSDP_SINGLE_AXIS_NAMES = (
+    MeshAxisName.DP_REPLICATE.value,
+    MeshAxisName.EDP_SHARD.value,
+)
+
+
+def dedicated_pg_backend_override(world_mesh: DeviceMesh):
+    """Backend override that opts a mesh axis out of full-world PG reuse.
+
+    ``DeviceMesh._init_one_process_group`` returns the default (WORLD) process
+    group -- not a new communicator -- for any mesh dimension (including one
+    produced by ``DeviceMesh._flatten``) whose ranks happen to span every rank,
+    as long as no explicit ``backend_override`` was given. FSDP's shard/replicate
+    axes can span every rank (e.g. ``dp_replicate`` alone under pure DDP, or
+    ``dp_shard * cp`` when ``dp_shard == 1``), and so can CP's own ``cp`` axis
+    when ``dp_shard == tp == pp == dp_replicate == 1``. Left alone, both would
+    reuse WORLD and share one NCCL communicator.
+
+    FSDP issues its all-gather/reduce-scatter from its own dedicated CUDA
+    streams, while CP's collectives run on the default/compute stream. Nothing
+    orders those two streams against each other, so the two collectives can be
+    enqueued in different host-side orders across ranks. Two collectives
+    sharing one communicator must be posted in the same order by every rank,
+    so a mismatched order deadlocks NCCL instead of merely serializing.

nodes.body:
Neither entry addresses the stated CP hazard:
- `dp_replicate` spans every rank only when `dp_shard == cp == tp == pp == 1`. That's pure DDP, where no CP collective exists to collide with. Under pure DDP this adds a dedicated world-size communicator (dense mesh, plus a second one in the sparse-mesh unflatten at L379) on a main-path config, with no hazard identified.
- `edp_shard = dp_shard*cp*tp/ep` is active only when `ep > 1` (`_axis_is_active`, L279-282), so it is always strictly smaller than the world and never aliases WORLD. The override there does nothing.

Suggest deleting `_FSDP_SINGLE_AXIS_NAMES` and the `elif` at L338, along with `test_pure_ddp_dp_replicate_group_is_dedicated`. The only case the PR's theory covers is the flattened `dp_shard * cp` axis in `resolve_fsdp_mesh`.

nodes.body:
This only works because two private upstream behaviors happen to line up. FSDP2 internally flattens with exactly `"_".join(names)`, and `DeviceMesh._flatten` returns the cached flattened mesh by name even though the later call passes no `backend_override`. If either detail changes upstream, the fix silently turns off and the regression test is the only signal.

Also, the underlying behavior ("a full-world mesh axis silently reuses WORLD unless you pass a backend override") belongs to DeviceMesh/FSDP2. Per CLAUDE.md principle 3, this needs a `TODO` linking a pytorch/pytorch issue. Better still, upstream should provide an option for FSDP2 or DeviceMesh to request a dedicated PG.

A side effect: `resolve_fsdp_mesh` is a resolver, and it now mutates the shared root mesh's flatten cache on every call (flux calls it twice, from `trainer.py:176` and `model.py:294`). *(unverified: re-flattening an already-flattened name with an override is a no-op on the pinned torch.)*

nodes.body:
Please drop this file from the PR. It demonstrates documented NCCL behavior: when ranks submit collectives to one communicator in different host orders, they deadlock. It doesn't demonstrate a torchtitan bug, and its own docstring says it is "not a natural FSDP prefetch repro" and "not a supported application pattern". It also has no consumer in the repo and calls `torch.cuda.*` directly. A gist linked from the PR description is enough.

Also note the separate-group "PASS" was measured with `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1`. The NVIDIA doc you link says reversed cross-communicator order can deadlock without implicit launch ordering. So the probe doesn't show that the fix is safe under default NCCL settings.

+"""Force a collective-order mismatch on two or more CUDA GPUs.
+
+  torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 scripts/repro_collective_order.py
+  torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=4 scripts/repro_collective_order.py --separate-group
+
+After matching warmup, rank 0 submits A2A then AG; peers submit AG then A2A.
+Shared groups should time out. Separate groups remove the matching conflict.
+This reversed-order schedule is diagnostic, not a supported application pattern.
+This is an intentional ordering-fault test, not a natural FSDP prefetch repro.
+Run each case separately with an external deadline; a timeout can abort CUDA.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+from datetime import timedelta
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--separate-group", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
+    dist.init_process_group("nccl", timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))
+    rank, world = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
+    elements = 1048576
+    assert world >= 2 and elements % world == 0
+    cp_group = dist.group.WORLD
+    fsdp_group = cp_group
+    if args.separate_group:
+        fsdp_group = dist.new_group(timeout=timedelta(seconds=30))
+    print(
+        f"rank={rank} shared={cp_group is fsdp_group} torch={torch.__version__} "
+        f"nccl={torch.cuda.nccl.version()} gpu={torch.cuda.get_device_name()} "
+        f"implicit={os.getenv('NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT', 'unset')}",
+        flush=True,
+    )
+    ag_input = torch.full((elements,), float(rank), device="cuda")
+    ag_output = torch.empty(elements * world, device="cuda")
+    ranks = torch.arange(world, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    a2a_input = (rank * world + ranks).repeat_interleave(elements // world)
+    a2a_output = torch.empty_like(a2a_input)
+    expected_ag = ranks.repeat_interleave(elements)
+    expected_a2a = (ranks * world + rank).repeat_interleave(elements // world)
+    ag_stream, cp_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    for warmup in (True, False):
+        order = ("ag", "a2a") if warmup or rank != 0 else ("a2a", "ag")
+        works = []
+        for operation in order:
+            print(f"rank={rank} warmup={warmup} submit={operation}", flush=True)
+            with torch.cuda.stream(ag_stream if operation == "ag" else cp_stream):
+                if operation == "ag":
+                    work = dist.all_gather_into_tensor(
+                        ag_output, ag_input, group=fsdp_group, async_op=True
+                    )
+                else:
+                    work = dist.all_to_all_single(
+                        a2a_output, a2a_input, group=cp_group, async_op=True
+                    )
+                works.append(work)
+            print(f"rank={rank} warmup={warmup} submitted={operation}", flush=True)
+        # Keep both Work objects and buffers alive; submit both before waiting.
+        for work in works:
+            work.wait()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(ag_output, expected_ag, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(a2a_output, expected_a2a, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        print(f"rank={rank} {'WARMED' if warmup else 'PASS'}", flush=True)
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+class TestFsdpCpCommunicatorIsolation(DTensorTestBase):
+    """Regression test for the CP/FSDP shared-communicator deadlock.
+
+    ``DeviceMesh._init_one_process_group`` reuses the default/WORLD process
+    group -- instead of creating a dedicated communicator -- for any mesh
+    dimension (including a flattened one) whose ranks span every rank, unless
+    an explicit ``backend_override`` is given. When ``dp_shard == 1``, CP's own
+    ``cp`` axis spans every rank, and so does the ``dp_shard * cp`` axis FSDP
+    shards parameters on, so both would silently collapse onto the same NCCL
+    communicator.
+
+    That matters because FSDP issues its all-gather/reduce-scatter from its
+    own dedicated CUDA streams, while CP's collectives run on the
+    default/compute stream. Nothing orders those two streams against each
+    other, so the two collectives can be enqueued in different host-side
+    orders across ranks -- and two collectives sharing one communicator must
+    be posted in the same order by every rank, so a mismatched order
+    deadlocks NCCL instead of merely serializing.
+
+    This guards ``resolve_fsdp_mesh`` and ``ParallelismContext.build_mesh``'s
+    fix: forcing a dedicated process group for FSDP's shard/replicate axes
+    whenever they could otherwise alias the default group.
+    """
+
+    @property
+    def world_size(self):
+        return 4
+
+    @with_comms
+    def test_pure_cp_fsdp_group_is_not_shared_with_cp_group(self):
+        """dp_shard=1, cp=world_size: the historically-buggy configuration."""
+        with patch(
+            "torchtitan.distributed.parallelism_context.device_type", self.device_type
+        ):
+            pd = ParallelismContext(
+                dp_replicate=1,
+                dp_shard=1,
+                cp=4,
+                tp=1,
+                pp=1,
+                ep=1,
+                world_size=4,
+                enable_sequence_parallel=False,
+            )
+            pd.build_mesh()
+
+            cp_group_name = pd.get_mesh("cp").get_group().group_name
+
+            storage_mesh, dp_mesh_dims = resolve_fsdp_mesh(pd)
+            assert dp_mesh_dims is not None
+            # Validate and resolve the shard group the way ``fully_shard`` does.
+            _validate_mesh(storage_mesh, dp_mesh_dims)
+            mesh_info = _get_mesh_info(storage_mesh, dp_mesh_dims)
+            fsdp_group_name = mesh_info.shard_process_group.group_name
+
+            self.assertNotEqual(
+                cp_group_name,
+                fsdp_group_name,
+                "CP and FSDP must not share a process group/communicator: "
+                "FSDP issues collectives on its own CUDA streams while CP "
+                "issues on the default/compute stream, so a shared "
+                "communicator can deadlock under cross-rank scheduling races.",
+            )
+
+    @with_comms
+    def test_pure_ddp_dp_replicate_group_is_dedicated(self):
+        """dp_replicate=world_size (pure DDP) must not alias the default group."""
+        with patch(
+            "torchtitan.distributed.parallelism_context.device_type", self.device_type
+        ):
+            pd = ParallelismContext(
+                dp_replicate=4,
+                dp_shard=1,
+                cp=1,
+                tp=1,
+                pp=1,
+                ep=1,
+                world_size=4,
+                enable_sequence_parallel=False,
+            )
+            pd.build_mesh()
+
+            default_group_name = dist.distributed_c10d._get_default_group().group_name
+            dp_replicate_group_name = pd.get_mesh("dp_replicate").get_group().group_name
+            self.assertNotEqual(default_group_name, dp_replicate_group_name)
+
+
 class _CausalAttentionReference(InnerAttention):

+def dedicated_pg_backend_override(world_mesh: DeviceMesh):
+    """Backend override that opts a mesh axis out of full-world PG reuse.
+
+    ``DeviceMesh._init_one_process_group`` returns the default (WORLD) process
+    group -- not a new communicator -- for any mesh dimension (including one
+    produced by ``DeviceMesh._flatten``) whose ranks happen to span every rank,
+    as long as no explicit ``backend_override`` was given. FSDP's shard/replicate
+    axes can span every rank (e.g. ``dp_replicate`` alone under pure DDP, or
+    ``dp_shard * cp`` when ``dp_shard == 1``), and so can CP's own ``cp`` axis
+    when ``dp_shard == tp == pp == dp_replicate == 1``. Left alone, both would
+    reuse WORLD and share one NCCL communicator.
+
+    FSDP issues its all-gather/reduce-scatter from its own dedicated CUDA
+    streams, while CP's collectives run on the default/compute stream. Nothing
+    orders those two streams against each other, so the two collectives can be
+    enqueued in different host-side orders across ranks. Two collectives
+    sharing one communicator must be posted in the same order by every rank,
+    so a mismatched order deadlocks NCCL instead of merely serializing.
+
+    Passing any explicit ``backend_override`` makes ``DeviceMesh`` create a
+    dedicated communicator instead of reusing WORLD. We pass the world mesh's
+    own backend config (e.g. real NCCL/Gloo, or "fake" under fake-mesh tests)
+    so this only changes communicator *identity*, not which backend is used.
+    """
+    return dist.get_backend_config(world_mesh.get_group())
+
+

inline_comments.body:
This explanation doesn't follow. The CUDA stream a collective is issued *from* has no effect on its *host* enqueue order. Host order is program order, and in torchtitan that's identical on every rank (FSDP hooks and CP calls run in the same Python sequence everywhere). For a single process group, ProcessGroupNCCL launches every collective on that PG's own NCCL stream, and NCCL serializes the operations of one communicator in launch order. So two collectives on one communicator can't be reordered on the GPU differently per rank. That's why the repro script has to force rank 0 to submit A2A before AG on the host.

If this docstring and the test docstring stay, they will teach a false model of NCCL semantics. Please either show the concrete rank-dependent host ordering that happens in a real run, or restate the rationale. *(unverified: the NCCL-internal serialization detail; a NCCL debug trace from the production hang would settle it.)*

inline_comments.body:
Neither entry addresses the stated CP hazard:
- `dp_replicate` spans every rank only when `dp_shard == cp == tp == pp == 1`. That's pure DDP, where no CP collective exists to collide with. Under pure DDP this adds a dedicated world-size communicator (dense mesh, plus a second one in the sparse-mesh unflatten at L379) on a main-path config, with no hazard identified.
- `edp_shard = dp_shard*cp*tp/ep` is active only when `ep > 1` (`_axis_is_active`, L279-282), so it is always strictly smaller than the world and never aliases WORLD. The override there does nothing.

Suggest deleting `_FSDP_SINGLE_AXIS_NAMES` and the `elif` at L338, along with `test_pure_ddp_dp_replicate_group_is_dedicated`. The only case the PR's theory covers is the flattened `dp_shard * cp` axis in `resolve_fsdp_mesh`.

inline_comments.body:
This only works because two private upstream behaviors happen to line up. FSDP2 internally flattens with exactly `"_".join(names)`, and `DeviceMesh._flatten` returns the cached flattened mesh by name even though the later call passes no `backend_override`. If either detail changes upstream, the fix silently turns off and the regression test is the only signal.

Also, the underlying behavior ("a full-world mesh axis silently reuses WORLD unless you pass a backend override") belongs to DeviceMesh/FSDP2. Per CLAUDE.md principle 3, this needs a `TODO` linking a pytorch/pytorch issue. Better still, upstream should provide an option for FSDP2 or DeviceMesh to request a dedicated PG.

A side effect: `resolve_fsdp_mesh` is a resolver, and it now mutates the shared root mesh's flatten cache on every call (flux calls it twice, from `trainer.py:176` and `model.py:294`). *(unverified: re-flattening an already-flattened name with an override is a no-op on the pinned torch.)*

inline_comments.body:
Please drop this file from the PR. It demonstrates documented NCCL behavior: when ranks submit collectives to one communicator in different host orders, they deadlock. It doesn't demonstrate a torchtitan bug, and its own docstring says it is "not a natural FSDP prefetch repro" and "not a supported application pattern". It also has no consumer in the repo and calls `torch.cuda.*` directly. A gist linked from the PR description is enough.

Also note the separate-group "PASS" was measured with `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1`. The NVIDIA doc you link says reversed cross-communicator order can deadlock without implicit launch ordering. So the probe doesn't show that the fix is safe under default NCCL settings.

inline_comments.body: The test imports `_get_mesh_info` and `_validate_mesh`, which are private FSDP2 internals, to re-derive the shard group. If the fix stays, a sturdier check is to call `fully_shard` on a tiny module with the resolved mesh and compare the group of the resulting `FSDPParamGroup`'s `mesh_info.shard_process_group` against the CP group. Or just assert that `storage_mesh[("dp_shard", "cp")]._flatten("dp_shard_cp").get_group()` is not the default group. Either way, the docstring above it repeats the stream/host-order rationale, which needs correcting (see the comment on `parallelism_context.py`).

reviews.body:
**Verdict: Request changes** -- the PR hasn't shown that the bug exists in torchtitan on `main`, and its explanation of the root cause doesn't match how a single NCCL communicator orders work. Isolating the groups could also bring in the cross-communicator ordering risk that the NVIDIA doc warns about.

**What this PR does.** When a mesh axis spans every rank, `DeviceMesh` reuses the WORLD process group instead of creating a new one. This PR passes an explicit `backend_override` so that FSDP's `dp_replicate`, `edp_shard`, and flattened `dp_shard*cp` axes get dedicated process groups. It pre-flattens `dp_shard_cp` under the name FSDP2 will use later, so FSDP2 picks the dedicated group out of the cache. It also adds two CPU tests and a manual NCCL probe script.

**Example.** `cp=4, dp_shard=dp_replicate=tp=pp=1` on 4 GPUs:
```
main: cp axis -> WORLD; FSDP shard axis dp_shard*cp (size 4) -> WORLD   (one communicator)
PR:   cp axis -> WORLD; FSDP shard axis -> new 4-rank PG                (two communicators)
```
The repro deadlocks only because rank 0 is forced to submit A2A->AG on the host while the other ranks submit AG->A2A. Torchtitan never does this, because its host order is the same on every rank. @fegin has run CP8 and CP16 with `dp_shard=1` many times without a hang. The author's answer is that the hang shows up with an *internal* CP implementation that uses P2P.

### Must fix
1. **The problem isn't shown on `main`.** @fegin's question ("what TorchTitan command / parallelisms") is still open: the only reported trigger is an out-of-tree CP. If that CP issues collectives in a rank-dependent host order (from a thread, data-dependent P2P, or lazily created P2P communicators), the fix belongs there. Please give either a torchtitan config that hangs, or an NCCL/flight-recorder trace from the production hang showing the mismatched sequence numbers across ranks.
2. `torchtitan/distributed/parallelism_context.py:95-100` -- the stream-based rationale is incorrect: the stream a collective is issued from doesn't change its host enqueue order, and one communicator serializes its work in launch order (inline).
3. **The fix may just move the hazard.** Once the groups are separate, the GPU order of FSDP and CP kernels really can differ across ranks. The linked NVIDIA doc says that can deadlock unless launch order is consistent or `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT` is set, and both measured runs set `NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1` (inline on the script).
4. `torchtitan/distributed/parallelism_context.py:77-80` -- the `dp_replicate` and `edp_shard` overrides don't address the CP case. The `dp_replicate` one adds a world-size communicator under pure DDP; the `edp_shard` one is a no-op (inline).
5. `torchtitan/distributed/fsdp.py:145-150` -- the fix depends on FSDP2's private flatten naming and on `DeviceMesh` caching by name, with no upstream TODO or issue (inline).
6. `scripts/repro_collective_order.py` -- remove it; it's a probe of documented NCCL behavior with no consumer in the repo (inline).

### Should consider
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_parallelism_context.py:22-25` -- the test re-derives the FSDP shard group using private FSDP2 helpers (inline).
- `parallelism_context.py:37-44` -- re-sorting `__all__` is unrelated to the fix.

### Questions
- In the production hang, which collectives were at the mismatched sequence number on each rank? Were both on PG 0, and was one of them a P2P op from the internal CP?
- If isolation is still wanted after (1) is answered, should a dedicated FSDP group become an option in FSDP2/DeviceMesh upstream rather than a pre-flatten trick here?

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Host order within one PG: FSDP2's pre-forward/pre-backward hooks and CP's attention collectives run on the main Python thread in the same program order on every rank. ProcessGroupNCCL launches every op of a PG on that PG's NCCL stream, waiting on the caller's current stream. Issuing from `all_gather_stream` instead of the compute stream changes the dependency, not the sequence number.
- If the change is still wanted after the root cause is established, the smallest version is just the `fsdp.py` pre-flatten with a TODO linking an upstream issue (~10 lines), with no `_FSDP_SINGLE_AXIS_NAMES`, no DDP test, and no script.
- After this PR, CP's `cp` axis still shares WORLD with `loss_mesh` (dp*cp) and grad-norm reductions. That is fine under same-order host submission, and it is the same argument for why the FSDP/CP share is fine as well.

</details>

Not verified: NCCL-internal serialization of one communicator across user streams; DeviceMesh flatten-cache behavior on the pinned torch; no GPU runs. A maintainer still needs to review.
